description.narrative: Central Asia faces significant risks from large-scale and cross-border emergencies such as natural disasters, climate change impacts, and dam and hydropower failings. These challenges cannot be managed by any single country alone and require strong regional, transboundary and international cooperation.In response, the governments of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, together with international partners, have established a Regional Forum of Heads of Emergency Authorities of Central Asian Countries (CESDRR). This forum serves as a permanent advisory platform to strengthen cooperation on disaster risk reduction (DRR), emergency prevention, and climate resilience.As a response to the various interventions in Kazakhstan after the 2024 floodings, the Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction and Surge Support (DRRS) has been asked to attend the Central-Asia Regional Forum to explore regional collaborations across Central Asia and strengthen regional and international cooperation in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, prevention and response to emergencies.The objective of this assignment is to strengthen existing collaboration with Kazakh counterparts and the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR), which have been established after the DRRS interventions in 2024 related to the Kazakhstan floods, and establish partnerships, and enhance the effectiveness of DRR implementation across Central Asia.
